21:1.sourceText: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν πάλιν Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Τιβεριάδος· ἐφανέρωσεν δὲ οὕτως.
21:1.targetText: After these things Jesus Himself again appeared to the disciples on the Sea of Tiberias, and He revealed Himself thus:

groups.note: Greek actively revealed/manifested Himself is recast as English appeared, with the same self-manifestation event retained.

The explicit Greek Himself belongs to the first self-manifestation and is the understood object of the repeated He revealed formula. LSV makes that self-reference explicit in both clauses; both English Himself mentions share the actual reflexive.

21:2.sourceText: ἦσαν ὁμοῦ Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος καὶ Ναθαναὴλ ὁ ἀπὸ Κανᾶ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ οἱ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ ἄλλοι ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο.
21:2.targetText: Simon Peter, and Thomas who is called Didymus, and Nathanael from Cana of Galilee, and the [sons] of Zebedee, and two of His other disciples were together.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article introduces Nathanaels from-Cana modifier; English gives the modifier directly without a separate who or article.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English sons explains the substantivized of-Zebedee patronymic; Greek has no printed sons noun at this point.

21:3.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς Σίμων Πέτρος Ὑπάγω ἁλιεύειν. λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ἐρχόμεθα καὶ ἡμεῖς σὺν σοί. ἐξῆλθον καὶ ἐνέβησαν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἐπίασαν οὐδέν.
21:3.targetText: Simon Peter says to them, “I go away to fish”; they say to him, “We go—we also—with you”; they went forth and immediately entered into the boat, and on that night they caught nothing.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds immediately before entered; this adverb is absent from the pinned N1904 verse.

21:4.sourceText: πρωΐας δὲ ἤδη γινομένης ἔστη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν· οὐ μέντοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.
21:4.targetText: And morning having now come, Jesus stood at the shore, yet indeed the disciples did not know that it is Jesus;

groups.note: Greek εἰς marks the shore location after the standing event; LSV describes that position as at the shore.

21:5.sourceText: λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς Ἰησοῦς Παιδία, μή τι προσφάγιον ἔχετε; ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ Οὔ.
21:5.targetText: Jesus, therefore, says to them, “Boys, do you have any meat?”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek μή marks a question expecting no; LSV asks do you have any meat without a separately expressed negative word.

sourceMoved.reason: Raw Greek 21:5 They answered Him No is rendered at the start of LSV 21:6; actual foreign-reference groups appear there.

21:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Βάλετε εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ πλοίου τὸ δίκτυον, καὶ εὑρήσετε. ἔβαλον οὖν, καὶ οὐκέτι αὐτὸ ἑλκύσαι ἴσχυον ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθους τῶν ἰχθύων.
21:6.targetText: They answered Him, “No”; and He said to them, “Cast the net at the right side of the boat, and you will find [some]”; they cast, therefore, and no longer were they able to draw it, from the multitude of the fishes.

groups.note: Greek εἰς marks the destination toward the right side; LSV renders at the right side.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English finding object is supplied; there is no some pronoun with find in Greek.

review.note: The opening They answered Him No belongs to raw Greek 21:5; the source witness remains at that original reference while English places the reply here.

21:7.sourceText: λέγει οὖν ὁ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ Ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν. Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος, ἀκούσας ὅτι ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν, τὸν ἐπενδύτην διεζώσατο, ἦν γὰρ γυμνός, καὶ ἔβαλεν ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν·
21:7.targetText: That disciple, therefore, whom Jesus was loving says to Peter, “It is the Lord!” Simon Peter, therefore, having heard that it is the LORD, girded on the outer coat (for he was naked), and cast himself into the sea;

groups.note: Actual dative article and first Peter name jointly supply to Peter as the saying recipient. The later nominative Peter subject remains a distinct original occurrence.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

21:8.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἄλλοι μαθηταὶ τῷ πλοιαρίῳ ἦλθον, οὐ γὰρ ἦσαν μακρὰν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἀπὸ πηχῶν διακοσίων, σύροντες τὸ δίκτυον τῶν ἰχθύων.
21:8.targetText: and the other disciples came by the little boat, for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away, dragging the net of the fishes;

21:9.sourceText: ὡς οὖν ἀπέβησαν εἰς τὴν γῆν, βλέπουσιν ἀνθρακιὰν κειμένην καὶ ὀψάριον ἐπικείμενον καὶ ἄρτον.
21:9.targetText: when, therefore, they came to the land, they behold a fire of coals lying [there], and a fish lying on it, and bread.

groups.note: The Greek lying-on compound describes the fish lying on the coal fire; English makes that implicit supporting object explicit as it within the same predicate.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English locative there is supplied with the fire lying; N1904 has no independent locative word there.

21:10.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐνέγκατε ἀπὸ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὧν ἐπιάσατε νῦν.
21:10.targetText: Jesus says to them, “Bring from the fishes that you caught now”;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

21:11.sourceText: ἀνέβη Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ εἵλκυσεν τὸ δίκτυον εἰς τὴν γῆν μεστὸν ἰχθύων μεγάλων ἑκατὸν πεντήκοντα τριῶν· καὶ τοσούτων ὄντων οὐκ ἐσχίσθη τὸ δίκτυον.
21:11.targetText: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net up on the land, full of great fishes—one hundred fifty-three; and though they were so many, the net was not split.

groups.note: Greek drew/pulled is rendered drew the net up in the shoreward movement context; English up belongs to that contextual pulling predicate, not a separately printed source adverb.

The Greek being-so-many genitive-absolute clause has concessive force here, rendered though they were so many; the whole circumstance construction supplies though without a separate Greek conjunction.

21:12.sourceText: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Δεῦτε ἀριστήσατε. οὐδεὶς ἐτόλμα τῶν μαθητῶν ἐξετάσαι αὐτόν Σὺ τίς εἶ; εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ Κύριός ἐστιν.
21:12.targetText: Jesus says to them, “Come, dine”; and none of the disciples were venturing to inquire of Him, “Who are You?” Knowing that it is the LORD;

21:13.sourceText: ἔρχεται Ἰησοῦς καὶ λαμβάνει τὸν ἄρτον καὶ δίδωσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τὸ ὀψάριον ὁμοίως.
21:13.targetText: Jesus, therefore, comes and takes the bread and gives [it] to them, and the fish in like manner;

groups.note: The written bread noun is the shared object of takes and gives; bracketed it repeats that same bread object in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds therefore after Jesus; no inferential connective occurs in the pinned N1904 verse.

21:14.sourceText: τοῦτο ἤδη τρίτον ἐφανερώθη Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν.
21:14.targetText: this [is] now a third time Jesus was revealed to His disciples, having been raised from the dead.

groups.note: Actual dative article and disciples noun jointly supply to ... disciples as the revelation recipients. The independently explained English His remains supplied rather than receiving a new source identity.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplies the nominal third-time statement; no finite is is written in Greek.
LSV supplies His with disciples; N1904 has no possessive pronoun there.

21:15.sourceText: Ὅτε οὖν ἠρίστησαν, λέγει τῷ Σίμωνι Πέτρῳ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Σίμων Ἰωάνου, ἀγαπᾷς με πλέον τούτων; λέγει αὐτῷ Ναί, Κύριε, σὺ οἶδας ὅτι φιλῶ σε. λέγει αὐτῷ Βόσκε τὰ ἀρνία μου.
21:15.targetText: When, therefore, they dined, Jesus says to Simon Peter, “Simon, [son] of Jonas, do you love Me more than these?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord; You have known that I cherish You”; He says to him, “Feed My lambs.”

groups.note: Actual dative article and Simon name jointly supply to Simon as the saying recipient. The following Peter name remains separately linked to its own actual dative occurrence, as do the later vocative Simon and personal pronouns.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Source-witness patronymic difference: N1904 has of John, Ἰωάνου, whereas LSV has of Jonas. These different names are not treated as an identical proper-name token.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English son explains the genitive patronymic; no son noun is printed in Greek.
LSV names Jonas as the father, where N1904 has John. The differing proper-name reading remains unpaired.

21:16.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ πάλιν δεύτερον Σίμων Ἰωάνου, ἀγαπᾷς με; λέγει αὐτῷ Ναί, Κύριε, σὺ οἶδας ὅτι φιλῶ σε. λέγει αὐτῷ Ποίμαινε τὰ προβάτιά μου.
21:16.targetText: He says to him again, a second time, “Simon, [son] of Jonas, do you love Me?” He says to Him, “Yes, Lord; You have known that I cherish You”; He says to him, “Tend My sheep.”

21:18.sourceText: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ὅτε ἦς νεώτερος, ἐζώννυες σεαυτὸν καὶ περιεπάτεις ὅπου ἤθελες· ὅταν δὲ γηράσῃς, ἐκτενεῖς τὰς χεῖράς σου, καὶ ἄλλος ζώσει σε καὶ οἴσει ὅπου οὐ θέλεις.
21:18.targetText: truly, truly, I say to you, when you were younger, you were girding yourself and were walking to where you willed, but when you may be old, you will stretch forth your hands, and another will gird you, and will carry [you] to where you do not will”;
